::: {.hero}
# Anoob Prakash
Postdoctoral Research Associate in plant genomics, climate adaptation, and bioinformatics
:::

## Profile

Researcher with training in plant biology, ecological and evolutionary genomics, climate adaptation, and computational analysis. Experience spans postdoctoral research, interdisciplinary collaboration, teaching, scientific writing, and restoration-focused applied genomics.

## Core Strengths

- Ecological and evolutionary genomics
- Climate adaptation and restoration science
- GWAS, genomic data analysis, and bioinformatics
- R, Unix/Linux, Tidyverse, ArcGIS
- Scientific communication, teaching, and data visualization

## Experience

### Purdue University — Postdoctoral Research Associate
2026–Present

- Investigates climate pre- or mal-adaptation using machine-learning approaches for species with high restoration potential.
- Identifies seed sources for regeneration planting in zones of mal-adaptation.

### University of Vermont — Graduate Research Assistant / Teaching Assistant
2018–2025

- Studied adaptive variation, introgression, and climate-associated traits in red spruce.
- Applied GWAS, Bayesian methods, and large-scale genomic and phenotypic analyses.
- Taught biology and ecology courses and trained students in R, lab methods, and research design.

### The Nature Conservancy — Graduate Research Intern
2021 & 2022

- Applied genomic-assisted seed sourcing to restoration planning.
- Supported post-planting evaluation across Virginia, West Virginia, and Maryland.

### Kerala Agricultural University — Research and Teaching Roles
2010–2016

- Conducted pollution biology research in forest tree species.
- Taught applied plant and forestry coursework and supported laboratory instruction.
